inline.s: Then the World-honored One answered in verse:
The blue and red and mixed colors — within the waves there is none at all,
‘The collector-karma’ is said of the mind, to awaken the ignorant common folk.
That karma has no existence at all; from the grasped of one’s own mind apart,
The grasped, and that which nothing grasps, with those waves are one and the same.
The body with its enjoyments and establishment, is the manifesting consciousness of beings,
In it all karmas are revealed, like the waves upon the water’s springs.”
Then the bodhisattva Mahamati again spoke a verse:
The nature of the great sea and its waves, heaving, can be distinguished;
The store and karma are even so; why are they not perceived and known?”
Ordinary beings, without wisdom, have the store-consciousness as the great sea,
The karma-marks are like its waves; by this simile the meaning is conveyed.”
The sun arises and its light shines equally on the low, the middle, and the high;
The Tathagata illumines the world, and for the foolish speaks the real,
Having divided all the dharmas, why does he not the real reveal?”
Then the World-honored One answered in verse:
If one speaks of the real, that mind itself has no reality.
Like the ocean’s waves, an image in a mirror, and a dream,
All these appear at once; the realm of the mind is the same.
Because the realms are not complete, karma turns and is born in due order,
Consciousness is what consciousness cognizes; the intellect, what the intellect intends,
The five are manifested, without any fixed sequence.
As a skilled painter, together with his pupils in the art,
Spread colors and depict all forms; so also do I speak my part.
The colors have no patterns in themselves; not the brush, nor the canvas white,
But to delight the living beings, they interweave and paint the many forms.
Words and speech are separately applied; the real is free of name,
Discrimination answers to the first acts; practice reveals the real.
The real is the place of self-awakening, where thought and its object are apart;
This for the Buddha’s sons is spoken; the foolish spread wide their discriminations.
All the various are like illusion; though they appear, no real is there,
And thus the many teachings, according to matters, are set forth here and there,
What is spoken is not that which is fit; and for such a one it is not speech.
To each and every patient, the good physician orders his prescription,
And the Tathagata, for the sake of beings, according to their minds speaks in due measure.
Deluded thought is not the realm, nor the portion even of the sravakas,
It is what the compassionate one speaks: the realm of self-awakening.
